stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec indicate no prior curation. Live preview in a CMS is complex: real-time rendering, state synchronization, multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) concerns. Openspec needed to elaborate requirements from scratch and propose technical depth; speckit needed to harden with testability, security, and edge-case criteria. Both agents assigned due to criticality and under-specification.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new Live Preview capability for Contentstack CMS content — no existing code implements this. The primary attachment point is useContent, the central hook through which 236+ components fetch content via getContentByKey. Any live preview integration must intercept/refresh content through this hook. Secondary attachment is the app bootstrap layer where Contentstack's Live Preview SDK would be initialized. Acceptance criteria are empty; VCs derived solely from the title/description and standard Contentstack Live Preview behavior. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs are framed to our side of the boundary.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with useful context about attachment points (useContent hook, contentstack service, app bootstrap). I created all 15 ACs from scratch based on: (1) openspec's notes identifying useContent as the central hook and the bootstrap layer as the initialization point, (2) standard Contentstack Live Preview SDK behavior (event-driven content updates, iframe/query-param detection), (3) the three-site scope. Key areas covered: initialization (AC-1), non-preview fallback (AC-2), real-time content refresh (AC-3, AC-4), irrelevant event handling (AC-5), SDK error resilience (AC-6), malformed data handling (AC-7), SSR safety (AC-8), type consistency (AC-9), cleanup (AC-10), rapid-event debouncing (AC-11), non-regression (AC-12), preview routing (AC-13), data isolation (AC-14), cross-site consistency (AC-15). CAVEAT: File contents were unavailable during this review. The actual implementation of useContent.ts and contentstack.ts may reveal existing patterns (e.g., caching, error handling) that warrant additional or refined criteria. I recommend reviewing those files before finalizing.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec provided architectural anchoring: identified useContent as the central hook (236+ components), the app bootstrap layer as the SDK initialization point, and correctly framed VCs on our side of the boundary due to unreachable Contentstack hosts. Speckit built 15 acceptance criteria from scratch covering initialization, fallback, real-time refresh, error resilience, SSR safety, debouncing, non-regression, and data isolation — leveraging openspec's context without duplicating it. However, speckit explicitly flagged that file contents (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts) were unavailable during review, meaning criteria were derived from architectural inference rather than actual implementation patterns. A human should verify the source files to ensure the proposed criteria align with existing caching, error-handling, and content-fetching patterns before implementation proceeds.
